Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Acme Insurance Holdings Third Quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Acme Insurance Holdings' Third Quarter 2024 earnings call. Joining me on the call today are Johnathan Hale, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Thompson, Chief Financial Officer; and Michael Chen, Chief Underwriting Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we are making today may be considered forward-looking. These statements are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause our actual results to differ materially from those projected. We encourage you to review our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks and uncertainties.

I will now turn the call over to Johnathan Hale.

Johnathan Hale: Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I'm pleased to report on Acme Insurance Holdings' performance for the third quarter. We delivered strong results, driven by meaningful improvements in our loss ratios through disciplined underwriting and proactive claims management, robust new business production reflecting our digital transformation and market positioning, a fortified capital position with substantial statutory surplus growth, and the continued effectiveness of our reinsurance program in mitigating volatility.

Sarah, our CFO, will now provide a more detailed review of our financial performance.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you, Johnathan. Good morning, everyone. As Johnathan mentioned, we had a solid quarter. Our net income was $450 million, or $3.20 per share. Key drivers of our financial performance included underwriting profitability and investment income gains. Our combined ratio was 92.4%, reflecting effective underwriting and claims management. We continue to maintain a strong capital position, with statutory surplus at $8.7 billion.

Let me unpack our results in more detail, starting with loss ratio trends and the key drivers behind them—specifically claims frequency and severity. This is a core metric for our property and casualty operations, and we've made meaningful progress here, reflecting the strength of our underwriting discipline and operational initiatives.

For the quarter, our consolidated ex-cat loss ratio improved to 61.8%, down 450 basis points from 66.3% in Q3 2023 and 120 basis points sequentially from Q2 2024. Including catastrophes—which totaled $285 million pretax, or 3.2 points on the loss ratio, driven primarily by Hurricane Idalia's impacts in the Southeast—this brings our full calendar-year-to-date ex-cat loss ratio to 62.4%, a robust 380 basis point improvement year-over-year. This positions us at the lower end of our targeted 60-64% ex-cat range for 2024, and well ahead of the industry average of around 68% as reported by AM Best for large P&C writers.

Breaking this down by the primary drivers: claims frequency—measured as claims per 100 exposure units—declined across most lines, thanks to a combination of favorable market conditions and our proactive interventions. In Personal Lines Auto, our largest book at 42% of earned premiums, frequency fell 8.2% year-over-year to 7.1 claims per 100 car-years. This reflects softer miles-driven post-COVID normalization, down 4% nationally per DOT data, and our Telematics Advantage program, now penetrating 28% of our policies—up from 19% last year. Usage-based insurance insights have allowed us to refine pricing algorithms, reducing accident likelihood by an estimated 12% for high-risk drivers via real-time coaching alerts.

Commercial Auto saw an even sharper drop of 11.5% to 5.4 claims per 100 vehicle-years, aided by our partnership with Geotab for fleet telematics, which flags risky behaviors like harsh braking. In contrast, Homeowners frequency ticked up modestly 2.1% to 4.8 claims per 100 policies, largely due to water damage claims amid wetter weather patterns in the Midwest.

Severity—the average cost per claim—remains the headwind, up 6.7% year-over-year to $4,820 across the portfolio. Inflation in repair costs, medical expenses, and litigation continues to pressure this metric, mirroring industry trends where ISO data shows auto physical damage severity up 9% and workers' comp medical severity up 7%. In Personal Auto, severity rose 9.4% to $5,210 per claim, driven by OEM parts inflation (up 15% per CCC Intelligent Solutions) and a 22% surge in used vehicle values stabilizing but still elevated. Liability severity in Commercial Lines climbed 8.1% to $12,450, fueled by social inflation—nuclear verdicts exceeding $10 million doubled in frequency per Thomson Reuters.

Property severity moderated to +4.2% at $18,700 per claim ex-cat, but cats amplified this, with Idalia wind/hail claims averaging $45,000—20% higher than 2023 analogs due to rising replacement costs (labor up 11%, materials up 8% per RSMeans data).

Geographically, our U.S. operations (85% of premiums) drove the improvement, with the ex-cat loss ratio at 60.9% versus 65.7% last year. The Southeast bore the brunt of cats, adding 5.1 points, but our Florida book—now just 2.1% of total homeowners exposure after 15% non-renewals in 2024—limited gross losses to $110 million. California wildfires were negligible this quarter, but we're monitoring exposure closely, having reduced it 18% via enhanced risk selection post-2023's McKinney Fire.

Internationally, our European renewal book (UK and Germany-focused) saw a loss ratio compression to 58.2%, benefiting from milder weather and our AI-powered claims triage reducing cycle time by 25%. In Asia-Pacific, via our joint venture with Ping An Insurance, severity pressures from Thailand flooding pushed the loss ratio to 65.4%, prompting a 7% rate increase at January renewals.

These trends aren't accidental—they stem from our multi-year tech roadmap. We've deployed Guidewire's ClaimCenter with embedded GenAI from Cytora, cutting manual adjudication by 35% and improving severity containment through predictive analytics that flags 15% of claims for early settlement. On the underwriting side, our EagleEye platform—integrating Verisk's catastrophe models and climate risk scores—has optimized our property book, shaving 2.2 points off the loss ratio via dynamic pricing tied to wildfire probability.

Reinsurance plays a key role too: Our $1.2 billion tower, renewed at favorable terms (17% net cost reduction), capped cat retention at 2.5 points for 1-in-100-year events, versus 3.8 points pre-2023. We've also diversified into specialty lines like cyber (loss ratio 55.2%) and parametric products, which grew 22% and provide frequency hedges.

Looking ahead, we expect Q4 ex-cat loss ratio in the low-62s, assuming no major cats, with frequency stabilizing and severity growth slowing to mid-single digits as supply chains normalize. Our pricing actions—averaging 9.8% increases across renewing business—coupled with 4% earned rate improvement, should sustain this trajectory. We're not complacent; social inflation risks persist, so we're piloting jury verdict prediction models with LexisNexis and expanding UBI to commercial fleets.

In summary, our loss ratio performance underscores the Acme difference: data-driven underwriting, tech-enabled claims, and disciplined exposure management. This supports our goal of a sub-62% calendar ex-cat loss ratio for 2025, driving ROE expansion toward 14%.

Turning now to new business production volume, a key leading indicator of our top-line growth trajectory and long-term embedded value creation. For the quarter, we delivered a robust $2.8 billion in Annualized Premium Equivalent from new business, up 18% year-over-year from $2.37 billion in Q3 2023. On a policy count basis, we wrote 1.45 million new policies, a 12% increase from 1.29 million last year, reflecting strong conversion rates across our distribution channels despite selective underwriting in a hardening market.

Breaking this down by segment, our diversified portfolio continues to drive balanced growth. In Life and Health, which accounted for 55% of total APE at $1.54 billion, we saw 22% YoY growth. Universal life products, particularly our Acme Vitality UL with embedded wellness incentives, contributed $850 million in APE, fueled by digital acquisition via our app-based platform—now boasting 4.2 million active users, up 30% YoY. Group health renewals with parametric riders added another $450 million, capitalizing on post-pandemic demand for flexible coverage amid rising healthcare inflation. Value of New Business margins here expanded to 28%, from 25% last year, thanks to improved lapse assumptions and higher investment yields on our backing fixed-income portfolio.

Shifting to Property & Casualty, representing 45% of APE at $1.26 billion, growth was 14% YoY. Commercial lines led with $720 million in APE, including a standout $250 million from cyber insurance expansions—our Acme CyberShield policy, underwritten with AI-driven risk modeling in partnership with CrowdStrike, saw 35% uptake among mid-market clients wary of ransomware trends. Personal lines added $540 million, driven by telematics-enabled auto policies (our DriveSafe bundle), where we issued 850,000 new policies, up 20%, with usage-based pricing reducing adverse selection by 15% based on our black-box data analytics.

Regionally, North America remains our powerhouse, delivering 60% of APE at $1.68 billion (20% YoY growth), bolstered by rate adequacy in California following the January wildfires and Florida hurricane rebuilds. We selectively grew homeowners exposure by just 8% in high-risk zones, prioritizing mitigation credits for policyholders with fortified roofs. Europe contributed 25% or $700 million (15% growth), with strength in the UK motor market post-Brexit rate normalization and our embedded insurance tie-ups with fintechs like Revolut, adding 250,000 policies. Asia-Pacific rounded out at 15% or $420 million (10% growth, but accelerating from flat in Q2), led by India life sales via bancassurance with HDFC Bank—our Prudence Endowment product hit $180 million APE—and pet insurance launches in Australia, tapping into a $2.5 billion TAM growing at 12% CAGR.

Key trends underpinning this performance include our digital transformation initiatives. Our AcmeOne omnichannel platform processed 65% of new business submissions, cutting cycle times to under 24 hours from 72, with straight-through processing rates at 82%—up from 65% last year—leveraging machine learning for fraud detection and automated underwriting. We've also embedded behavioral economics into product design, like gamified loyalty in term life, boosting conversion by 18%. Strategically, we're leaning into climate-resilient and cyber products, allocating 20% of our $500 million innovation budget to parametric triggers for nat-cat events, mirroring Allstate's FloodSmart model but with satellite data from Planet Labs for real-time indexing.

Looking forward, we guide to full-year 2024 new business APE of $11.5-12.0 billion, implying 16-20% growth, with VNB margins stable at 26-28%. This positions us well against peers like Chubb and AXA, who reported 12-14% growth last quarter, as our tech edge and risk-adjusted pricing sustain profitability in a volatile environment—think secondary perils up 25% per Swiss Re sigma data. Retention on new business cohorts is tracking at 92%, validating our quality focus.

Next, I'd like to provide a detailed update on our capital position and statutory surplus levels, which remain a cornerstone of our financial strength and strategic flexibility in this dynamic insurance landscape. As you know, in the property & casualty and life & health sectors, maintaining robust statutory capital under NAIC guidelines is critical for regulatory compliance, reinsurance capacity, and shareholder returns—especially amid elevated catastrophe activity and interest rate volatility we've seen in 2024.

Our consolidated statutory policyholders' surplus stood at $8.7 billion as of September 30, 2024, reflecting a solid 11.8% year-over-year increase from $7.8 billion at year-end 2023. This growth outpaced our book-grown peers like Travelers and Chubb, driven by a combination of strong underwriting profitability, favorable reserve development, and disciplined capital deployment. Excluding the $450 million after-tax benefit from prior-year loss reserve releases—primarily in our commercial auto and workers' comp lines—organic surplus growth was still a healthy 8.2%.

On the risk-based capital front, our total RBC ratio improved to 528% of company action level, up from 492% at the end of 2023 and well above our internal target of 450% and the NAIC's 200% regulatory trigger. This positions us in the top quartile among AM Best-rated "A+" carriers, giving us ample dry powder for growth initiatives. For context, our life & health subsidiaries maintained an RBC of 465%, bolstered by stable morbidity trends in group health post-COVID.

Breaking down the drivers of surplus growth, retained statutory earnings contributed $620 million year-to-date, fueled by a combined ratio of 92.4%—our best since 2019—and net investment income of $410 million, up 22% YoY thanks to higher reinvestment yields in a rising rate environment. Our fixed-income portfolio, which comprises 72% of invested assets ($12.4 billion total), now yields 4.2% on a book-value basis, with duration managed at 5.1 years to balance income and interest rate risk. Unrealized gains flipped positive by $280 million in Q3 alone, as the Bloomberg Aggregate Bond Index rebounded 5.8% amid Fed pivot signals, reversing 2023's $1.2 billion headwind.

We also saw tailwinds from $320 million in favorable prior-year development, with 65% coming from our P&C segments: specifically, $150 million in auto physical damage from better-than-expected subrogation recoveries, and $110 million in general liability from asbestos resolution patterns aligning with industry trends observed at peers like CNA Financial. Offsetting this modestly were $210 million in catastrophe losses, dominated by Hurricane Idalia and California wildfires, which equated to 2.4 loss ratio points—below our 10-year average of 3.8 points.

Regionally, our U.S. operations drove 78% of surplus growth, with Southeast P&C surplus up 15% to $3.2 billion, reflecting rate adequacy gains of 9.2% in homeowners amid Florida OIR-approved hikes. However, we proactively ceded 25% more Florida wind risk to our quota-share treaties with reinsurers like Swiss Re and RenaissanceRe, maintaining gross probable maximum loss at 12% of surplus. In the Midwest, commercial lines surplus grew 10%, supported by multi-peril crop reinsurance placements that mitigated drought impacts. Internationally, our Bermuda-domiciled reinsurer added $180 million to surplus via excess-of-loss treaties on European motor business, where claims inflation eased to 4.1% from 7.2% in 2023. Asia-Pacific life operations, focused on unit-linked products similar to Prudential's offerings, contributed $90 million, though we trimmed Taiwan earthquake exposure by 15% through cat bond issuances totaling $250 million—our first foray into insurance-linked securities, yielding a blended 6.8% return.

Looking at trends and forward indicators, our statutory surplus has compounded at a 10.4% CAGR over the past five years, outstripping nominal GDP growth and even premium growth at 9.1%. This resilience held through the 2023 capital markets stress test, where our RBC dipped only to 475% under a +200bps yield shock scenario—far superior to the peer median of 420%. Leverage remains conservative: debt-to-surplus at 18.2% (target <25%), with $1.2 billion in junior surplus notes qualifying as Tier 2 capital under NAIC revisions. We continue to optimize via ORSA modeling, stress-testing for a 1-in-250-year cat event (e.g., $5 billion industry-wide California quake) that would leave RBC at 410%.

Strategically, this capital fortress enables multiple levers. First, returns to shareholders: We repurchased $550 million in common stock (4.2% of float) at an average of $48.20 per share, accretive by 8% to book value per share, which ended the quarter at $52.40. Our board approved a 12% dividend hike to $1.28 annual, payable quarterly, targeting a 45-50% payout ratio on operating EPS. Second, M&A and organic expansion: We deployed $300 million into bolt-on acquisitions, including a $180 million workers' comp block from a regional mutual, mirroring W.R. Berkley's playbook for embedded value. Pipeline remains active for cyber and D&O runoff portfolios. Third, technical initiatives: We're advancing our capital efficiency program, including dynamic financial analysis under NAIC's updated principles-based reserving for life products, which we expect to unlock $150 million in surplus by 2026. We've also layered in collateralized reinsurance with Lloyd's syndicates, reducing ceded premiums by 8% while preserving 95% recovery rates.

Risks and outlook: Near-term, we monitor credit spread widening—our NAIC 1-2 municipals (65% of bonds) held steady, but a repeat of 2023's inversion could pressure OTTI charges. Cat outlook is elevated, with Atlantic basin ACE index at 120% of normal YTD; we've fortified with $4.1 billion in reinsurance towers, 40% collateralized. Longer-term, IFRS 17 transition for our Canadian ops will contractually service margin surplus by $200 million at adoption, but we've pre-funded via a $100 million surplus note issuance.

In summary, our $8.7 billion surplus and 528% RBC underscore Acme's premier capital position, positioning us to navigate volatility, seize growth in high-return lines like excess & surplus, and deliver superior TSR.

Finally, as we review our Q3 results, one of the key pillars of our risk management framework is the effectiveness of our reinsurance program. In an industry where volatility from catastrophes and emerging risks like cyber and climate change can swing earnings dramatically, our reinsurance strategy has once again proven resilient, delivering strong protection to our balance sheet while optimizing capital efficiency.

Our program, renewed effectively on January 1st this year amid a hardening reinsurance market, maintains a diversified tower across property catastrophe excess-of-loss, casualty quota share, and facultative layers, with total reinsurance capacity of approximately $15 billion equivalent ultimate net loss. Our lead markets include longstanding partners like Swiss Re, Munich Re, and Berkshire Hathaway Reinsurance Group, complemented by a broad panel of 25 reinsurers to mitigate counterparty risk—our top five represent just 42% of gross ceded premiums, down from 48% last year.

Turning to the numbers, our reinsurance program delivered exceptional results in Q3. Gross written premiums across our P&C and specialty lines grew 8% year-over-year to $2.7 billion, with ceded premiums at $542 million—a stable 20.1% cession rate, aligned with our target range of 18-22%. This reflects disciplined underwriting, avoiding over-ceding in non-volatile lines like our U.S. commercial auto book.

On the loss recovery side, we recovered $1.2 billion against $1.5 billion in gross ultimate losses, achieving a robust 80% recovery rate—up 5 percentage points from Q3 2023. This directly contributed to our net combined ratio of 92.4%, a 310 basis point improvement from the gross ratio of 95.5%, and well below our long-term target of under 96%. Excluding cats, the net loss ratio stood at 61.2%, benefiting from $180 million in favorable prior-year development, 85% of which was supported by reinsurance recoverables.

A key highlight was our Cat XL program's performance during the quarter's $450 million industry loss events, including Hurricane Idalia remnants and European windstorm Babet. Our program attached at $250 million ENL per occurrence for U.S. Northeast wind and $180 million for European named storms, with full reinstatement provisions. We ceded 92% of these losses, limiting net retention to just $35 million—far below our risk appetite. Year-to-date, catastrophe losses net of reinsurance were $620 million, or 23% of gross, compared to the industry's 35% average per AM Best data.

Looking at trends, our five-year average recovery rate has improved to 78% from 72% in 2019, driven by enhanced cat modeling and claims triangulation. We've integrated RMS v18 and AIR Worldwide's latest climate-adjusted models into our pricing and accumulation analyses, reducing modeled probable maximum loss by 12% on our U.S. homeowners portfolio. This has allowed us to negotiate better terms: our 2024 Cat XL pricing rose only 8% despite 25% industry hardening, thanks to our strong loss history and diversified geographic footprint.

Regionally, the program shines brightest in high-exposure areas. In North America, which accounts for 55% of our gross probable maximum catastrophe loss, reinsurance covered 95% of our $1.1 billion Eastern U.S. hurricane PML, critical amid an active 2024 Atlantic season projected by NOAA at 17 named storms. Europe, at 22% of PMCL, benefited from our multi-year quota share with Hannover Re, ceding 30% of our D&O and cyber writings—key as cyber claims surged 40% per Munich Re's sigma report. In Asia-Pacific, our 15% cession on Japan earthquake risk via a Tokyo Marine-led layer performed flawlessly during Typhoon Gaemi, with zero net impact.

We've invested heavily in technical enhancements to future-proof the program. This year, we launched a $25 million digital reinsurance platform with reinsurer input, automating bordereaux reporting and collateral calls—reducing settlement times from 45 to 12 days and disputes by 60%. We're also pioneering alternative risk transfer: in June, we issued our first $150 million cat bond via a Bermuda SPV, targeting California wildfire risk with a parametric trigger tied to Verisk's WildfireIQ index. This diversifies away from traditional capacity, which tightened post-2023 Maui fires, and lowers our all-in cost of protection by 15 bps.

Strategically, we're positioning for a market where reinsurance rates are expected to soften modestly in 2025 per Guy Carpenter's outlook, but with capacity gaps in retrocession layers. Our focus remains on quota share optimization—expanding casualty QS from 20% to 25% cession next year to smooth volatility in our U.S. workers' comp book, where OSHA claims are up 18% amid labor shortages. Counterparty monitoring is rigorous: 100% collateralization on unauthorized reinsurers, with no rated below A- by S&P, and stress-tested for a 1-in-200-year event.

In summary, our reinsurance program not only shielded earnings—contributing $280 million to bottom-line profitability in Q3—but also unlocked $450 million in capital release under Solvency II and RBC frameworks through efficient risk transfer. This positions us exceptionally well for 2025 growth targets of 10% premium expansion with sub-95% net combined ratios.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator: Thank you. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from David Klein with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

David Klein: Good morning, thanks. Can you provide more color on the claims severity trends, particularly in liability lines, and how you're addressing social inflation?

Sarah Thompson: Good morning, David. Absolutely, severity remains a focus area, up 6.7% year-over-year to $4,820 across the board, with liability in commercial lines up 8.1% to $12,450, driven by social inflation where nuclear verdicts over $10 million have doubled per Thomson Reuters data. We're tackling this head-on with pilots on jury verdict prediction models alongside LexisNexis, and expanding our UBI programs to better select risks. Pricing increases of 9.8% on renewals, combined with tech like Cytora's GenAI for early settlements, are helping contain it. We see severity growth moderating to mid-single digits in Q4 as supply chains ease.

Operator: Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Lisa Chen: Good morning. Could you discuss the impact of elevated catastrophe activity, like the Atlantic basin's above-normal season, on your business and reinsurance recoveries?

Michael Chen: Good morning, Lisa. Cats have been a factor, with $285 million pretax in Q3, adding 3.2 points, mainly from Idalia. Our reinsurance tower capped net retention effectively—92% ceded on those events, limiting impact to $35 million net. Year-to-date, net cats are 23% of gross versus industry's 35%, thanks to our $15 billion capacity and diversified partners. We're monitoring NOAA's 17-storm projection closely, with PMLs controlled via Verisk models and recent cat bond issuance.

Operator: Our next question comes from Robert Patel with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Robert Patel: Thanks, good morning. On new business, how sustainable is the 18% APE growth, especially in cyber and parametric lines amid market volatility?

Sarah Thompson: Morning, Robert. Very sustainable, driven by our tech platforms like AcmeOne achieving 82% STP. CyberShield with CrowdStrike grew 35%, tapping ransomware fears, and parametrics up 22% as hedges. Retention at 92% on cohorts validates quality. We guide 16-20% full-year growth, outpacing peers, with VNB margins at 26-28% thanks to risk-adjusted pricing.

Operator: Our next question is from Emily Rodriguez with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Emily Rodriguez: Good morning. Regarding capital, with RBC at 528%, what's the plan for deployment between buybacks, dividends, and M&A?

Sarah Thompson: Hi Emily. We're balanced: $550 million in buybacks this year, accretive to BVPS now at $52.40, and a 12% dividend increase to $1.28 annual. M&A pipeline active, like the $180 million workers' comp bolt-on, with more in cyber runoffs. Surplus growth of 11.8% gives flexibility, stress-tested to 410% RBC in worst-case cats.

Operator: Thank you. That concludes the question queue. I'll now turn the call back over to the executive team for closing remarks.

Johnathan Hale: Thank you for your questions and your interest in Acme Insurance Holdings. In closing, we are confident in our ability to continue delivering strong results and creating value for our shareholders. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
